feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for a senior digital communications/platform leader with clear domain focus and solid public-sector experience. It shows breadth and progression well, but it is somewhat dense, repetitive, and could sharpen impact by reducing overlap and adding more outcome-focused achievements.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear positioning: the headline, summary, and experience consistently support a strong niche in digital platforms, governance, analytics, and communications leadership.  
- Credibility and progression: long tenure at NACo with promotions signals trust, growth, and increasing responsibility.  
- Good use of scale indicators: metrics like “10,000+ page website,” “3.5 million annual page views,” and “50+ internal publishers” strengthen impact.

1. Top improvements  
- Reduce duplication: “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT” overlap heavily; consolidate to improve structure and scannability.  
- Add more results, not just responsibilities: several bullets say “led,” “supported,” or “strengthened” without quantifying business/user outcomes.  
- Fix style consistency: use consistent punctuation in lists and bullets; “social, and multimedia” has an unnecessary comma; “organization-wide” vs. “organization’s” usage varies; “Ranked among the top public universities…” is weak/irrelevant filler for education. No major misspellings found.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible intro with clear seniority and domain focus. It’s slightly dense and overlaps with the subtitle, core competencies, and work experience; adding one concrete scale cue would increase impact.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Tighten phrasing and reduce list-like density: “Senior digital leader with 12+ years building platforms, governance, and content operations for high-volume public-sector communications.”
- Add a concrete scale/result drawn from recent experience, e.g. “Led modernization of a 10,000+ page Drupal site serving 3.5M annual page views.”
- Replace “Leads” with a parallel noun phrase or past/present-tense structure for smoother style consistency.
- Consider sharper positioning: “enterprise web modernization, analytics, editorial systems, and AI-enabled search/content experiences” rather than “multimedia production” if space is tight.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Digital Platform & Communications Systems Leader” already covers positioning; avoid repeating too many capability labels from the subtitle.
- The capability list closely mirrors Core Competencies; keep the intro focused on value proposition and scale, not exhaustive skills.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes that align with the headline and recent roles, but the section is broad and overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and work experience. Tightening wording and emphasizing higher-value leadership areas will improve impact.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use slightly sharper, more executive phrasing: Enterprise web modernization • Digital governance and editorial operations • Analytics, dashboards and reporting systems • Cross-channel communications leadership
- Replace generic terms with clearer outcomes/scope: AI-enabled search and content discovery • Workflow automation and platform integrations • Public-sector advocacy communications • Multimedia, studio and livestream production
- Standardize style: spell out “and” instead of mixing “&” with other constructions, and keep all items parallel noun phrases
- Consider reducing to 6–7 items to avoid sounding repetitive and to prioritize most marketable strengths

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Significant overlap with the header summary and Topline Skills; this section should stay high-level and not repeat tool-specific detail
- “Multi-channel communications operations” and “Advocacy and public-sector communications” partially duplicate multiple NACo role bullets
feedback.footer:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant project snapshot, but it reads dense and repeats themes already covered in Work Experience and skills. Tightening phrasing and standardizing style will improve scanability and impact.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Add dates or “Selected Recent Projects” framing, and keep each item to one crisp outcome-focused line.
- Standardize parallel structure: start each project with a strong verb and use consistent punctuation/capitalization.
- Replace vague phrasing like “designed for continued campaign growth” with sharper language such as “built for reuse and expansion.”
- Consider this tighter version: AI Hybrid Search — Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience using hybrid retrieval, vector search, structured content workflows, and bill-level AI chat to improve policy discovery. We Are Counties Microsite — Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, downloadable resources, and a reusable modular architecture. Organization Anniversary Campaign — Developed a multi-part digital campaign featuring editorial storytelling, archival media, web features, and a 10×20-foot interactive conference display. Advocacy Video Series — Launched a recurring advocacy video series spanning editorial planning, production, and distribution across web, email, and social.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- AI Hybrid Search, microsite work, and advocacy video overlap with Work Experience bullets; keep this section shorter and more portfolio-like.
- “AI-enabled,” “workflows,” and “campaign” recur frequently across the CV.

items.title: Coleman DAVIS
items.subtitle: Digital Platform & Communications Systems Leader
items.content: Senior digital leader with 12+ years of experience building the platforms, governance models and content operations behind high-volume public-sector communications. Leads enterprise web modernization, analytics infrastructure, editorial systems, multimedia production and AI-enabled user experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations.

items.title: Email
items.content: colemandavis4@gmail.com

items.title: Website
items.content: https://colemanpdavis.com/

items.title: Core Competencies
items.content: Enterprise website modernization • Digital governance & editorial systems • Analytics and reporting infrastructure • Multi-channel communications operations • AI-enabled search and content experiences • Workflow automation and platform integration • Advocacy and public-sector communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations

items.title: CV Footer
items.content:
### Recent Projects
**AI Hybrid Search**
Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience combining hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search and bill-level AI chat to improve discovery of complex policy content.
**We Are Counties Microsite**
Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, downloadable resources and a modular structure designed for continued campaign growth.
**Organization Anniversary Campaign**
Developed a multi-part digital campaign combining editorial storytelling, archival media, web features and a 10×20-foot interactive conference display connected to the main site.
**Advocacy Video Series**
Built a recurring advocacy video program spanning editorial planning, production and distribution across website, email and social channels.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with good scope, but it reads as a task list and overlaps heavily with the header, skills, and project section. Tighten it around 3–5 high-impact contributions and add outcomes, scale, or deliverables.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper lead: “Embedded full-time as strategic communications consultant for a U.S. national membership organization, leading digital platform improvements, campaign delivery, and content operations.”
- Combine overlapping bullets on systems/workflows/governance into one impact-oriented line: “Improved cross-channel communications operations by redesigning web workflows, analytics, and governance across web, email, social, and multimedia.”
- Make Drupal/CMS work more outcome-based: mention number of sites/pages, campaign launches, toolkit downloads, publishing speed, or stakeholder groups supported.
- Rephrase AI bullet to emphasize leadership and product value: “Led AI-enabled search initiative, defining retrieval approach, structured content model, and discovery UX for complex policy/member content.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled search” and microsite work already appear in Recent Projects; keep this entry higher-level and reserve specifics there.
- Avoid repeating generic governance/analytics language already covered in the summary and NACo roles.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with solid scale metrics. It would be sharper if the opening were more concise and if channel oversight bullets emphasized outcomes, not just scope.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the opener with: “Directed NACo’s digital media function, leading web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget strategy for a high-volume public-sector communications operation.”
- Tighten the web bullet: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page website to Drupal, supporting 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Recast channel oversight toward impact: “Oversaw email and social programs reaching tens of thousands of county officials, strengthening advocacy communications and audience engagement.” Add open/click/growth metrics if available.
- Combine infrastructure/operations wins: “Built NACo’s first in-house broadcast studio and expanded analytics across GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery, improving reporting, production capacity, and decision-making.”
- End with governance outcome language: “Established publishing standards and cross-department planning systems to improve consistency, speed, and accountability.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Email/social/video operations” overlaps with the 2018–2022 NACo role; keep this entry focused on enterprise-scale leadership and transformation.
- Video-program growth also appears in Recent Projects and earlier NACo roles; emphasize studio build and organizational capability here.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid progression story, but this entry overlaps heavily with the later Director role and earlier Digital Media Manager role. Make it more clearly about executional leadership, editorial operations, and channel growth during this period.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper scope statement: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social and video, supporting advocacy messaging and cross-team editorial execution.”
- Tighten bullets around distinct contributions: managed 4 weekly newsletters; produced/scaled weekly advocacy video update; coordinated editorial planning across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Replace soft phrasing like “helped scale,” “helped improve,” and “strengthened” with direct ownership where accurate: “standardized publishing workflows,” “led editorial coordination,” “expanded.”
- Add measurable outcomes if available: newsletter audience/open rates, video cadence/views, publishing volume, number of teams/stakeholders coordinated.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Digital communications across web, email, social and video” is already prominent in the Director role; keep this version more tactical and operations-focused.
- Weekly video updates also appear in the 2015–2018 role and Recent Projects; avoid repeating “established video” unless this role clearly expanded it.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it overlaps heavily with the header, Core Competencies, and recent NACo bullets. Tighten it to emphasize senior leadership scope and audience/governance strengths without repeating generic “digital strategy” language.

Suggested edit
- Replace with sharper, less repetitive phrasing:
- Enterprise web and content strategy
- Editorial governance and publishing systems
- Cross-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy communications
- Audience and stakeholder content planning
- Consider swapping “Multi-channel” to “Cross-channel” for a more executive tone.
- “Messaging” is weaker than “communications” here; it sounds narrower and less operational.
- If you want more impact, make one line outcome-oriented: “Governance models for high-volume publishing” or “Content strategy for complex stakeholder audiences.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Enterprise digital strategy” and “Editorial systems and governance” duplicate the header and Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” overlaps with Core Competencies; rephrase to avoid repeating “advocacy/public-sector communications” exactly.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it reads like a raw tool list and overlaps heavily with the Technical + IT section. For a topline skills item, emphasize higher-value platform leadership and modernization themes over individual technologies.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: Drupal and enterprise CMS modernization • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript) • API and platform integrations • Workflow automation and Airtable-based systems • AI-enabled search and discovery experiences
- Drop lower-priority or older items unless they are target-role keywords: WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages, and jQuery.
- Group tools into capability language rather than listing every platform; this better matches recent experience in Drupal modernization, integrations, and AI search.
- If space allows, add one impact cue tied to recent work elsewhere, e.g., “supporting large public-facing sites and structured content workflows.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item duplicates the Technical + IT section almost exactly; keep Topline Skills broader and let Technical + IT hold the full tool inventory.
- “CMS modernization,” “workflow automation,” and “AI-enabled search experiences” also echo Core Competencies; avoid repeating the same phrasing verbatim.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster for recent leadership roles, but it reads as a tool dump and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” analytics section. Make it more outcome-oriented and slightly more strategic.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: “GA4, BigQuery, Power BI, Looker Studio and Microsoft Clarity • Analytics infrastructure and dashboarding • KPI framework design • Executive/leadership reporting • SEO, UX and performance analysis”
- Group tools first, then capabilities; this improves scanability and positions you as someone who builds insight systems, not just uses platforms.
- Replace “optimization” with clearer capability language like “UX and performance analysis” unless you can support testing/CRO work elsewhere.
- If space allows, add one strategic phrase tied to recent work: “measurement strategy” or “decision-ready reporting.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This substantially duplicates “Analytics and reporting infrastructure” in Core Competencies and “Data, Analytics & Optimization” in Technical + IT.
- Consider shortening this section or using it to emphasize strategy/reporting rather than repeating the same tools.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This skill block is relevant, but it reads generic and overlaps heavily with “Multimedia production and livestream operations” in Core Competencies and several NACo bullets. Make it more specific to current senior-level capability, not task-level production.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe toward leadership + delivery: “Broadcast-quality video production • Livestream and hybrid event delivery • In-house studio operations • PTZ camera and multi-camera workflows • Virtual event production”
- Replace “Video production and editing” with a broader, more senior phrase like “Broadcast-quality video production” or “End-to-end video production”
- Combine “Livestreaming” and “Hybrid and virtual event production” to reduce fragmentation and improve scan value
- If accurate, add one stronger differentiator: “In-house studio buildout and operations” or “Advocacy video programming”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Multimedia production and livestream operations” already appears in Core Competencies; consider shortening one of the two or making this section more tool/workflow-specific
- “Studio operations” and “PTZ camera systems” are supported by the NACo role, so avoid repeating those exact phrases elsewhere without added context

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it’s too bare and duplicates the “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” topline skills section. Use this item to signal depth and recency, with Drupal clearly leading.

Suggested edit:
- Reorder by relevance/recency: **Drupal (enterprise migration, microsites)** • **WordPress** • **SharePoint** • **Power Pages** • **GitHub Pages**
- If space allows, add light qualifiers instead of just names: **Drupal 10, WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages, GitHub Pages**
- Consider renaming the heading to **CMS & Web Platforms** for cleaner phrasing.
- If you want more impact, replace the list with: **Drupal (10,000+ page migration; custom microsites), WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages, GitHub Pages**

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This overlaps heavily with **Topline Skills → Web Platforms & Technical Execution**; avoid repeating the exact same list in both places.
- Since Drupal is already strongly evidenced in recent roles/projects, don’t overstate older or less central platforms unless you’ve used them meaningfully.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. Tighten it to emphasize implementation-level tools most relevant to recent work.

Suggested edit:
- Rename/refocus toward execution: “Front-End & Technical Implementation” or “Web Development & Deployment.”
- Use cleaner, current phrasing: “HTML/CSS” instead of “HTML5 • CSS3”; keep “JavaScript,” and only retain “jQuery” if still actively used in recent projects.
- Group by function for readability: “HTML/CSS • JavaScript • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions.”
- If accurate, add one outcome-oriented qualifier elsewhere or in project bullets, e.g., “used for microsite builds, tagging, lightweight serverless functions, and deployment automation.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Duplicates “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already listed under Topline Skills.
- “Google Tag Manager” may fit better under Analytics/Optimization unless you specifically use it for technical implementation.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow systems capability. It also overlaps with “Workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” already called out elsewhere, so this item should be tighter and more role-relevant.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from a raw list to grouped systems: “Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier • Project/work management: Jira, Asana, Trello, Basecamp • Collaboration: Slack, Microsoft Teams”
- If space allows, add light functional context: “workflow automation, intake/tracking, cross-team coordination”
- Prioritize strongest/recently relevant tools first; keep Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier prominent given the CV’s emphasis on systems and automation
- Consider renaming the heading to “Workflow Automation & Collaboration Tools” for clearer alignment with the experience section

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable systems” and “Workflow automation” already appear in Topline Skills; avoid repeating the same phrasing here
- Slack/Teams are common collaboration tools; keep them only if they support the workflow-systems framing rather than padding the list

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it reads as a generic software inventory rather than evidence of capability. Since email leadership already appears in recent NACo roles, this item should stay concise and emphasize systems breadth, not repeat newsletter management.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Member Engagement Platforms**
- Reorder by likely relevance/recency and standardize naming: **Higher Logic • Microsoft Dynamics 365 Customer Insights – Journeys • Mailchimp**
- If accurate, add scope in brief parentheticals: **Higher Logic (member communications/community) • Dynamics 365 Customer Insights – Journeys (automation/journey orchestration) • Mailchimp (campaign email)**
- If one platform was primary, move the strongest/most recent tool first to signal depth rather than a random list.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Avoid adding “email newsletters” or audience-size claims here; those are already covered in Work Experience.
- “Engagement” overlaps with broader multi-channel communications language elsewhere, so keep this item tool-specific.

items.title: Data, Analytics & Optimization
items.content: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • Looker Studio • Power BI • BigQuery • SEO • A/B testing • Dashboarding
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this item is too generic and largely duplicates the stronger “Analytics, Insights & Optimization” topline skills section. In Technical + IT, make it more tool-specific and trim broad capability terms.

Suggested edit:
- Replace with: **GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • BigQuery • Looker Studio • Power BI • Google Search Console • Google Optimize / A/B testing tools**
- Remove vague nouns like **Dashboarding**; that’s a capability already implied by Looker Studio/Power BI and covered elsewhere.
- If accurate, swap **SEO** for a concrete platform/tool (e.g., **Google Search Console**, **Screaming Frog**, **SEMrush**) to make the list more technical.
- Order by strongest/recently evidenced tools from recent roles: **GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, BigQuery** first.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item overlaps heavily with **Topline Skills → Analytics, Insights & Optimization**; keep Topline for capabilities and this section for tools only.
- **A/B testing** may feel unsupported unless referenced in experience; keep only if you’ve used it directly.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid progression story, but this reads broadly and overlaps with the stronger 2018–2024 NACo entries. Tighten it to emphasize foundational impact, promotion, and distinct early-career contributions.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to foreground advancement and team-building: “Promoted across two digital roles to help establish NACo’s first in-house digital team…”
- Make the scope concrete and concise: “Supported web, email, social, and multimedia operations; improved publishing workflows during a major website refresh.”
- Separate production impact from management: “Produced livestreams and launched/ran weekly video updates” and “provided day-to-day oversight to a digital media associate.”
- Add metrics if available: number of livestreams/events, video cadence/audience, website size/traffic at the time, or workflow efficiency gains.

Possible rewrite
- Promoted across two digital roles to help build NACo’s first in-house digital team, supporting web, email, social, and multimedia operations.
- Contributed to a major website refresh, improved publishing workflows, produced livestreams and weekly video updates, and provided day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 advocacy video bullet; distinguish this as the earlier launch/build phase.
- Avoid repeating broad workflow language already used in later NACo roles unless you add a specific early accomplishment.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry that shows initiative, especially the first podcast launch. It should be tightened and framed around outcomes or “firsts,” while avoiding overlap with later NACo digital/media roles.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to emphasize scope and standout contribution: “Coordinated county innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo programs and policy priorities.”
- Make the digital work more concise and achievement-led: “Produced digital and multimedia content for organizational communications, including launching NACo’s first podcast from concept through scripting and production.”
- If possible, add one measurable outcome: number of episodes, audience growth, stakeholder reach, or types of research/projects supported.
- Consider splitting into 2 bullets rather than one paragraph for readability and clearer impact.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Avoid broad phrases like “digital content production and multimedia materials,” which overlap with later digital/media roles.
- Don’t overstate leadership in digital strategy here; later NACo roles already establish that progression more strongly.

items.title: Multimedia & Creative Tools
items.content: Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream studio workflows • Podcast production
items.aiFeedback:
